html:
Shewa (Shoa) is a region of the central Ethiopian highlands, around today's Addis Ababa. The map shows a territory of this name from 1279 to 1400, placed east of the highlands towards the lowlands of the Horn.

In those years Shewa was a frontier between Christian and Muslim powers. A Muslim Sultanate of Showa ruled parts of it until about 1285, when the rising Walashma rulers of Ifat absorbed it. At the same time the Christian prince Yekuno Amlak took power in 1270 from a base in Amhara and Shewa and founded the Solomonic dynasty of the Ethiopian Empire.

His grandson Amda Seyon I defeated Ifat in 1332, and Shewa became a heartland of the Christian empire. Ifat's heirs regrouped further east as the Adal Sultanate.
sum: Shewa (Shoa) is a region of the central Ethiopian highlands, around today's Addis Ababa. The map shows a territory of this name from 1279 to 1400, placed east of the highlands towards the lowlands of the Horn.
